ai.literal: To those who are strong, opposing, avoid; without avoiding, against those who are weak, let hostility proceed.
ai.translation: Avoid opposing those who are stronger than you; but against those who are weaker, do not avoid, and let your hostility proceed.
ai.modern: வலிமை உடையவர்களுடன் எதிர்த்துப் போரிடுவதைத் தவிர்க்க வேண்டும்; ஆனால், வலிமை குறைந்தவர்கள் மேல் பகை கொள்வதைத் தவிர்க்காமல், அப்பகையை மேற்கொள்ள வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet offers a pragmatic strategy for dealing with conflict based on the relative strength of the opponent. It advises that one must strictly avoid confronting or opposing those who are stronger, as such a conflict is self-destructive. Conversely, when dealing with those who are weaker, one should not hesitate or avoid conflict, but rather let the hostility proceed to resolve the issue or establish dominance. The contrast between 'ōmpuka' (avoid) for the strong and 'ōmpā' (not avoiding) for the weak highlights this realistic approach to power dynamics.

words.gloss: he who does not enjoy or share

ai.literal: One who has no love, one who has no abundant allies, and who himself does not enjoy or share, how will he ward off the enemy's strength?
ai.translation: How can a man who has no love in his heart, no powerful allies to support him, and who does not himself enjoy or share his resources, ever withstand the strength of his enemy?
ai.modern: அன்பு இல்லாதவனாகவும், சிறந்த துணை இல்லாதவனாகவும், தானும் அனுபவிக்காதவனாகவும் இருப்பவன், தன் பகைவனுடைய வலிமையை எவ்வாறு வெல்ல முடியும்?
ai.explanation: This couplet describes the vulnerability of an isolated and miserly person against an adversary. A person who lacks love cannot win the hearts of others, and without noble allies, he stands alone. Furthermore, if he is selfish and does not enjoy or share his resources, he remains weak and friendless. The poet asks rhetorically how such a person can ever ward off the strength of an enemy.

words.gloss: one who is easy to defeat

ai.literal: One who fears, knows not, harmony has not, gives not, is easily vulnerable to enemies.
ai.translation: One who is fearful, ignorant, lacking in social harmony, and miserly, becomes an extremely easy prey for his enemies.
ai.modern: அச்சப்படுபவனும், அறிவில்லாதவனும், பிறருடன் இணங்கிப் போகாதவனும், கொடைத்தன்மை இல்லாதவனும் ஆகிய ஒருவன், தன் பகைவர்க்கு மிக எளிதில் தோற்றுப் போகக்கூடியவன் ஆவான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines four fatal flaws that make a person highly vulnerable to their enemies. First, fearfulness prevents them from taking bold action. Second, ignorance deprives them of strategic wisdom. Third, a lack of harmony or adaptability isolates them from potential allies. Fourth, miserliness ensures they have no loyal supporters. Together, these traits make such a person an incredibly easy target for any adversary.

ai.literal: He who does not rid himself of anger, who has no self-control, at all times, in all places, to anyone, is easy.
ai.translation: One who does not rid himself of anger and lacks self-control is easy for anyone to defeat, at any time and in any place.
ai.modern: கோபத்தை விடாதவனும், மன அடக்கம் இல்லாதவனுமாகிய ஒருவன், எக்காலத்திலும், எவ்விடத்திலும், யாருக்கும் எளிதில் வெல்லக்கூடியவன் ஆவான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines the fatal vulnerabilities of an undisciplined adversary. A person who cannot free themselves from anger (வெகுளி) and lacks the strength of self-control (நிறை) becomes entirely predictable and weak. Because of these internal flaws, they can be easily conquered by any opponent (யார்க்கும்), at any given time (எஞ்ஞான்றும்), and in any location (யாங்கணும்). Their emotional instability deprives them of strategic defense, making them an easy target.

ai.literal: The consequence he does not consider, proper things he does not do, disgrace he does not consider, good character he lacks—to enemies (he is) easy.
ai.translation: One who does not consider the consequences of his actions, does not do what is proper, does not fear disgrace, and lacks good character is an easy prey for his enemies.
ai.modern: செயலின் விளைவை ஆராயாதவன், நன்மையானவற்றைச் செய்யாதவன், பழிக்கு அஞ்சாதவன், நற்பண்புகள் இல்லாதவன் ஆகிய இவன் தன் பகைவர்களுக்கு மிக எளியவன் ஆவான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines the flaws that make a person highly vulnerable to their adversaries. First, such a person does not look ahead to the consequences of their actions ('வழி நோக்கான்'). Second, they fail to perform deeds that are proper or beneficial ('வாய்ப்பன செய்யான்'). Third, they are indifferent to the disgrace or blame their actions might bring ('பழி நோக்கான்'). Finally, they lack basic good character ('பண்பிலன்'). A person with these four defects becomes an effortless target ('இனிது') for their enemies ('பற்றார்க்கு') to overcome.

ai.literal: The enmity of him who has blind anger and him who has excessively great lust is fit to be desired.
ai.translation: The hostility of one who has blind, unreasoning anger and excessive, uncontrolled lust is a state to be welcomed and desired by his adversaries.
ai.modern: ஆராய்ந்து பார்க்காத குருட்டுத்தனமான கோபத்தை உடையவன், அளவற்ற பேராசை உடையவன் ஆகியோரது பகையானது (அவர்களை எளிதில் வெல்லலாம் என்பதால்) விரும்பத்தக்கதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains whose enmity is advantageous to seek or welcome. A person who is blinded by anger ('காணாச் சினத்தான்') cannot think rationally or assess situations. Similarly, one driven by excessive lust or desire ('கழிபெருங் காமத்தான்') is easily distracted and weakened by his passions. Their hostility ('பேணாமை') is to be welcomed ('பேணப் படும்') because their inherent flaws make them easy to defeat, turning their enmity into an opportunity for their rivals.

ai.literal: Even by giving, to secure is necessary surely, of him who, staying close, does improper things, the enmity.
ai.translation: One must surely resolve, even by making concessions, the enmity of a person who stays close but performs improper deeds.
ai.modern: நெருங்கி இருந்து தகுதியற்ற செயல்களைச் செய்பவனுடைய பகையை, ஏதேனும் கொடுத்தாவது தீர்த்துக் கொள்ள வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet advises on how to handle the hostility of an untrustworthy person who is physically close but acts improperly. Such a person, being nearby, can cause immense harm through their unfit actions. Therefore, the poet emphasizes that one must surely neutralize or buy off their enmity, even if it requires giving away wealth or making concessions. Resolving this threat immediately is crucial because an enemy within close proximity is highly dangerous.

ai.literal: If one is without good qualities, has many faults, and becomes without allies, it possesses great security for his enemies.
ai.translation: If a person has no good qualities, possesses many faults, and lacks any allies, he becomes an easy target, offering a great advantage and security to his enemies.
ai.modern: ஒருவன் நற்குணங்கள் இல்லாதவனாய், பல குற்றங்களை உடையவனாய், துணையாக இருக்கும் சுற்றத்தாரும் இல்லாதவனாய் இருந்தால், அது அவனுடைய பகைவர்களுக்குப் பெரும் பாதுகாப்பாக அமைந்துவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines the traits that make an opponent extremely vulnerable and easy to conquer. When a person lacks virtuous qualities and is burdened with numerous flaws, they naturally fail to win the trust of others. Consequently, they end up completely isolated without any allies or supporters to defend them. This state of utter weakness and friendlessness provides a great sense of security and an effortless victory to their enemies.

ai.literal: To those who fight, far will not depart joy, wisdom lacking, fearing enemies if they obtain.
ai.translation: If one obtains enemies who lack wisdom and are easily frightened, joy will never depart far from those who oppose them.
ai.modern: அறிவில்லாத, பயப்படுகின்ற பகைவர்களைப் பெற்றால், அவர்களை எதிர்த்துப் போரிடுபவர்களுக்கு மகிழ்ச்சி எப்போதும் நீங்காமல் நிலைத்திருக்கும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains the strategic advantage of facing weak adversaries. If a person's enemies are both foolish and cowardly, defeating them becomes an effortless task. Consequently, those who oppose such weak enemies will experience constant success and happiness. The phrase 'cēṇ ikavā iṉpam' beautifully conveys that joy will never go far away from them, as victory is guaranteed.

ai.literal: The trivial matter of an unlearned man's anger, at all times, him who does not yield to it, will not join, glory.
ai.translation: Glory will never abide with one who does not know how to yield to and defuse even the trivial anger of an unlearned man.
ai.modern: அறிவில்லாதவன் கோபப்படும் எளிய விஷயத்தைக்கூடத் தவிர்த்துக்கொள்ள உடன்படாதவனிடம், அவனது புகழானது எப்போதும் நிலைத்து நிற்காது.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains that the anger of an unlearned or ignorant person is a trivial matter ('சிறுபொருள்'). However, a wise leader must know how to handle or yield ('ஒல்லுதல்') to such situations to avoid unnecessary conflict. If a person is stubborn and does not yield to or defuse even such minor provocations, their glory ('ஒளி') will depart from them forever ('எஞ்ஞான்றும் ஒல்லாது'). True greatness lies in knowing when to overlook the petty anger of the ignorant.
